message.content:
Let  
\[
A_0=\arcsin\frac35,\qquad B_0=\arcsin\frac{24}{25}.
\]
Since \(\sin A=\frac35\), \(A\) can be \(A_0\) or \(\pi-A_0\).  
Since \(\sin B=\frac{24}{25}\), \(B\) can be \(B_0\) or \(\pi-B_0\).

We also need \(A+B<\pi\) for a triangle. Since \(A_0<B_0\), the valid cases are:

1. \(A=A_0,\ B=B_0\):
\[
\sin C=\sin(A+B)=\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B
\]
\[
=\frac35\cdot\frac7{25}+\frac45\cdot\frac{24}{25}
=\frac{21}{125}+\frac{96}{125}
=\frac{117}{125}.
\]

2. \(A=A_0,\ B=\pi-B_0\):
\[
C=\pi-A-B=B_0-A_0
\]
so
\[
\sin C=\sin(B_0-A_0)
=\sin B_0\cos A_0-\cos B_0\sin A_0
\]
\[
=\frac{24}{25}\cdot\frac45-\frac7{25}\cdot\frac35
=\frac{96}{125}-\frac{21}{125}
=\frac{75}{125}
=\frac35.
\]

Thus the possible values are \(\frac{117}{125}\) and \(\frac35\).

The answer is \(\frac{117}{125}, \frac35\).
